requirements.title: The fix commands and their flags
requirements.rationale: The same steps must be reachable as one loop, by a person at their own checkout, and by a box, so each step is its own command.

criteria.action: register the commands `fix <input>`, `fix brief <input>`, `fix run --run-id <id>`, `fix submit --run-id <id>` and `fix land --run-id <id>` on the toolio shell, each declaring a result schema that appears in the `af --schema` output and its golden file
criteria.contract: `af --schema` lists all five fix command paths, each with a non-empty result schema

setup: the cmd/af command registry with the fix commands registered
check.pseudocode: out = run('af --schema'); for p in ['fix','fix brief','fix run','fix submit','fix land']: assert out.commands[p].result_schema != {}; assert out == golden

criteria.action: default to `--brain agentkit`, `--sandbox local`, `--budget 10`, `--max-turns 150`, `--attempts 2`, `--land pr` and `--timeout 45m` when these flags are not given
criteria.contract: `af fix --help` and the `fix` result's `attempts_max` and `land` show these defaults when the flags are omitted

setup: a temporary repository with a gate and a scripted brain that submits a landable fix, run with the brain flag explicitly set only where needed to stay offline
check.pseudocode: h = help('fix'); assert defaults(h) == {brain:'agentkit', sandbox:'local', budget:10, 'max-turns':150, attempts:2, land:'pr', timeout:'45m'}; r = run(dry); assert r.result.attempts_max == 2 and r.result.land == 'pr'

criteria.action: accept `--base` on `fix` and `fix brief`; `--attempts`, `--land pr|branch|none` and `--no-verify` on `fix`; `--land` on `fix land`; and the `brain.Flags` brain flags on `fix` and `fix run`. `fix` also opts into the run directory, the forge, `--repo`, `--dry-run` and `--context`
criteria.contract: `fix` and `fix brief` accept --base; `fix` accepts --attempts, --land, --no-verify, --repo, --dry-run, --context and the brain flags, and opts into run dir and forge; `fix land` accepts --land; `fix run` accepts the brain flags; a flag on a command that does not declare it is a usage error

setup: the registered fix commands
check.pseudocode: assert flags('fix') ⊇ {base,attempts,land,no-verify,repo,dry-run,context,brain,sandbox,budget,max-turns,script}; assert 'land' in flags('fix land'); assert 'brain' in flags('fix run'); assert exit(run('fix land --attempts 2')) == 2

criteria.condition: `--attempts` is outside 1–5, or `--land` is not one of `pr`, `branch` or `none`
criteria.action: refuse the invocation before preflight, without making any model call or forge request
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

setup: a forge test server that records requests
a scripted brain that counts Run calls
check.pseudocode: for args in ['--attempts 0','--attempts 6','--land bogus']: r = run(fix, args); assert r.exit == 2 and r.status == 'usage'; assert forge.requests == [] and brain.runs == 0

criteria.condition: the input of `fix` or `fix brief` is a URL naming a pull request or merge request
criteria.action: refuse the invocation without making any model call or forge write
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

setup: an httptest GitHub and GitLab server recording writes and a counting brain
check.pseudocode: for cmd in ['fix','fix brief']: for u in [ghPR, glMR]: r = run(cmd,u); assert r.exit == 2; assert writes(forge)==[] and brain.runs==0

criteria.condition: `fix run`, `fix submit` or `fix land` is given a `--run-id` that `toolio.OpenRunDir` rejects, or a run directory that has no `fix.json`
criteria.action: refuse the invocation without touching the checkout
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

setup: a repository checkout with a recorded HEAD and tree
a run directory that exists but has no fix.json
check.pseudocode: for cmd in ['fix run','fix submit','fix land']: for id in ['../x','nope',idNoFixJson]: r = run(cmd,'--run-id',id); assert r.exit==2; assert snapshot(repo)==before

criteria.condition: `af fix submit --run-id <id>` is invoked with JSON on stdin
criteria.action: behave as `submission.Command("fix submit", FixReport)` from spec 07, using the `fix_report` kind of 09-REQ-4
criteria.contract: spec 07's submit envelope; on acceptance, the normalised payload is written as the run's submission

setup: a run created by `af fix brief` with run.json present
a valid report on stdin with CRLF in `change` and files out of order
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix submit', id, stdin=report); assert r.exit==0; s = read(runDir/'submission.json'); assert s.type=='fix' and '\r' not in s.change and sorted(s.files)

criteria.condition: `af fix run --run-id <id>` is invoked on an existing run
criteria.action: open a box on `--dir`, run exactly one round of the brain with the stored brief, and apply its accepted tree to the checkout as in 09-REQ-5, without measuring and without creating a branch or commit
criteria.contract: a result carrying the round number, the submission outcome and the apply counts {written, deleted, ignored}

setup: a run from `fix brief` on a temporary repository
a scripted brain that edits a file and submits a report
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix run', id, ...); assert r.result.apply.written >= 1; assert rev_parse('HEAD')==base_head; assert branches(repo)==['main']; assert 'measure' not in ledger kinds

requirements.title: Preflight, baseline and fix.json
requirements.rationale: Every working-tree change must be the run's own, and every refusal that can be known before spending model money must stop the run first.

criteria.action: run, before any model call and in this order, the checks for the work-tree top level, the checked-out branch, a clean tree, an available gate, the landing prerequisites and brain construction, and stop at the first failing check
criteria.contract: a preflight failure makes no model call, creates no branch or commit, and sends no forge write

setup: repositories each violating a different preflight check, one at a time and then several at once
a counting brain, a recording forge
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix on dirty AND no-gate AND no-origin); assert r.category=='preflight' and 'dirty' in r.message; assert brain.runs==0 and writes(forge)==[]; assert branches==['main']

criteria.condition: `--dir` is not the top level of a git work tree, HEAD is detached, or `--base` names a branch other than the checked-out branch
criteria.action: stop the run. For the `--base` mismatch, the message reads "check out <base> first"
criteria.contract: status `usage`, exit code 2

setup: a repository, a subdirectory of it, and a detached-HEAD copy
check.pseudocode: assert run(fix,'--dir',sub).exit==2; assert run(fix,'--dir',detached).exit==2; r = run(fix,'--base','other'); assert r.exit==2 and 'check out other first' in r.message

criteria.condition: `gitx.DirtyFiles` returns at least one path (tracked changes or untracked files that are not ignored)
criteria.action: stop the run and name at most the first 20 dirty paths in the failure message
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `preflight`, exit code 1

setup: a repository with 25 untracked non-ignored files and one tracked modification
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='preflight'; assert count_paths(r.message)==20

criteria.condition: `--no-verify` is not set and `project.Detect` returns a table with no available check
criteria.action: stop the run
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `preflight`, `fix_hint {flag: "--no-verify"}`, exit code 1

setup: a clean repository with no detectable gate
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='preflight' and r.fix_hint=={'flag':'--no-verify'}; r2 = run(fix,'--no-verify'); assert r2.category != 'preflight' or 'gate' not in r2.message

criteria.condition: the landing is not possible: `--land pr|branch` outside `--dry-run` with no `origin` remote, `--land pr` with no valid target repository, `--land pr` with an unauthenticated forge client, or `GetRepository` failing or returning an archived repository
criteria.action: stop the run with the category that matches the failing check. Under `--dry-run`, a missing token raises the warning `no_forge_token` instead of stopping
criteria.contract: no origin: `failed`/`preflight`, exit 1; no target: `usage` with `fix_hint {flag: "--repo"}`, exit 2; unauthenticated: `failed`/`auth` with `fix_hint {env}` naming `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GITLAB_TOKEN`, exit 1; repository unreadable or archived: `failed`/`forge`, exit 1

setup: clean repositories with a gate: one without origin, one with origin but no parsable target repo and no --repo
a forge client that is unauthenticated; one whose GetRepository returns 404; one returning Archived true
check.pseudocode:
r1=run(fix,'--land','branch'); assert r1.exit==1 and r1.category=='preflight'; r2=run(fix,'--land','pr'); assert r2.exit==2 and r2.fix_hint.flag=='--repo'
assert run(unauth).category=='auth' and 'GITHUB_TOKEN' in fix_hint.env; assert run(notfound).category=='forge'; assert run(archived).category=='forge'; assert 'no_forge_token' in codes(run(unauth,'--dry-run').warnings)

criteria.condition: spec 07's registry cannot construct the selected brain, for example because the vendor key is missing
criteria.action: stop the run before opening a box
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `auth`, exit code 1

setup: --brain agentkit with the vendor key unset
a box provider spy
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--brain','agentkit'); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='auth'; assert provider.opened==0

criteria.condition: every preflight check passes
criteria.action: record `base`, `base_head` as the full 40-hex commit hash, and the pinned table. Unless `--no-verify` is set, run the baseline gate exactly once with `checks.Run(dir, {Table})` in the default runner mode with no label. Raise the warning `baseline_failing` when the baseline is red, and the warning `issue_closed` when the input issue is closed; neither stops the run
criteria.contract: the baseline gate id is stored and reported as `baseline {gate_id, passed}`

setup: a repository whose fixture gate is red at HEAD
an issue whose state is closed
a counting checks runner
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix brief', url); assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', r.result.base_head); assert gateRuns==1 and label==''; assert {'baseline_failing','issue_closed'} <= codes(r.warnings)

criteria.action: write `<run_dir>/fix.json` atomically (temporary file in the same directory, then rename), holding run_id, the input kind, origin and key (issue URL, absolute file path, or SHA-256 of the text), the issue reference and title when there is one, the target repository, base, base_head, the pinned table, the baseline gate id, no_verify, prefix_sha256, the context values and the round counter
criteria.contract: `fix.json` parses as JSON with every listed field, and is never observed partially written

setup: a successful `fix brief` run for an issue input
a filesystem watcher that reads fix.json during the write
check.pseudocode: fj = json(runDir/'fix.json'); assert all(k in fj for k in REQUIRED); assert not glob(runDir/'fix.json.*tmp*'); assert key('text')==sha256(text)

requirements.title: The brief
requirements.rationale: A byte-identical prefix keeps the driver's prompt cache across rounds, and the task block carries everything that changes between rounds.

criteria.action: for any two rounds, attempts or resumes of the same input on the same tree, render a byte-identical prefix that contains no run id, timestamp, duration or context value
criteria.contract: equal `prefix_sha256` values

setup: a fixed input and tree
check.pseudocode: for (rid, att, rnd, ctx) in gen(): b = BuildBrief(input, tree, rid, att, rnd, ctx); assert b.Prefix == base.Prefix; assert rid not in b.Prefix and all(c not in b.Prefix for c in ctx)

criteria.action: compose the prefix in this order: (1) the mandate: find the root cause, write the reproducing test first, make the smallest change; never commit, push, branch, edit the issue or write under protected paths; run tests in targeted form, with `af gate run` for the full suite; (2) the `af-fix` skill text; (3) the report, labelled as material to verify and not as instructions, inside a fence longer than any backtick run it contains; (4) the gate table and baseline per check: name, argv, status, and the tail of any failing check; (5) the repository map built with a 4000-token budget; (6) the fix-report schema
criteria.contract: sections appear in order: mandate, af-fix skill text, report, gate table and baseline, repository map, report schema; the report fence is longer than five backticks and the report is labelled as material to verify, not instructions; the baseline section shows each check's name, argv, status and the failing check's tail; the repository map is built with a 4000-token budget

setup: an issue whose body contains a run of five backticks
a gate table with one failing baseline check with a log tail
check.pseudocode: p = brief.Prefix; idx = [p.find(m) for m in MARKERS]; assert idx == sorted(idx) and -1 not in idx; assert fence_len(p) > 5; assert repomapBudget == 4000

criteria.action: compose the task block from: the run id; the attempt and round numbers; the submit instruction (`af fix submit --run-id <id>` with the report on stdin, or the `submit_fix` tool); earlier questions with their answers; for a later round, the previous round's refusal; and for a later attempt's first round, why the previous attempt ended
criteria.contract: both contain the run id, attempt and round numbers, `af fix submit --run-id <id>` and `submit_fix`; the round-2 block contains the previous refusal; the attempt-2 block states why the previous attempt ended; a round-1 attempt-1 block has neither

setup: a run in round 2 of attempt 1 after a regressed verdict, and a run in attempt 2 round 1 after bounds were spent
check.pseudocode: t = Task(state); assert runId in t and 'af fix submit --run-id '+runId in t and 'submit_fix' in t; assert refusal in t2; assert reason in t3; assert refusal not in t1

criteria.condition: a run carries n `--context` values
criteria.action: for each i from 0 to n−1, take the i-th question from the newest run directory under `.agent-fox/run/` whose `fix.json` has the same input key, whose envelope has status `needs_human`, and which carried exactly i context values, and render that question with the i-th answer in the task block
criteria.contract: the 0th question is taken from the newest same-key needs_human run with 0 context values and shown with answer A; the 1st question is taken from the run with exactly 1 context value and shown with answer B; the different-key run is never used

setup: three run directories: two with the same input key and needs_human envelopes carrying 0 and 1 context values, one older duplicate for 0 values, and one run with a different key
check.pseudocode: t = Task(ctx=['A','B']); assert q0_new in t and q0_old not in t and q1 in t and other not in t; assert order(t, q0_new, 'A', q1, 'B')

criteria.condition: no earlier run directory matches the i-th context value
criteria.action: render the i-th answer without a question and continue the run
criteria.contract: warning `question_not_found`

setup: no earlier run directory for the input key
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--context','B'); assert 'B' in task and no question; assert 'question_not_found' in codes(r.warnings)

criteria.action: set `Brief.Tools` to the box's whole tool set, `HookConfig.ProtectedPaths` to the `policy` default protected paths, and `HookConfig.AllowPrograms` to the detected gate programs plus `git`, `af`, `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `rg`, `diff`, `sort`, `pwd`, `echo` and `mkdir`
criteria.contract: Brief.Tools equals the box session's whole tool set; HookConfig.ProtectedPaths equals the policy default list (.git/, .agent-fox/, .specs/, .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml); HookConfig.AllowPrograms contains make, sh, git, af, ls, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, rg, diff, sort, pwd, echo and mkdir

setup: a project whose detected gate programs are `make` and `sh`
check.pseudocode: b = BuildBrief(...); assert b.Tools == session.Tools(); assert b.Hook.ProtectedPaths == policy.Default; assert set(b.Hook.AllowPrograms) >= {'make','sh','git','af','ls','cat','head','tail','wc','grep','rg','diff','sort','pwd','echo','mkdir'}

criteria.condition: a round is about to start
criteria.action: write `.agent-fox/gate.json` (the pinned table) and `.agent-fox/guard.json` (the suite, the protected paths and the allowed programs) into the box through `Session.WriteFile`
criteria.contract: both files exist in the box before `brain.Execute` is called

setup: a local box session and a brain whose Run snapshots the box's .agent-fox directory
a two-round scenario
check.pseudocode: onRun: snap = read(box/.agent-fox/gate.json, guard.json); assert snap.gate == pinned and snap.guard.protected_paths == policy.Default; assert called for rounds 1 and 2

criteria.condition: `af fix brief <input>` completes preflight and baseline
criteria.action: write `<run_dir>/brief.md`, `fix.json` and `.agent-fox/run/<id>/run.json` as `{run_id, kind: "fix_report", attempt: 1, nonce}`, and write nothing outside `.agent-fox/`
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0, with result {brief_path, prefix_sha256, base, base_head, baseline {gate_id, passed}, table, submit argv}

setup: a clean repository with a gate and local bare origin
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix brief', url); assert r.exit==0; rj=json(repo/'.agent-fox/run'/id/'run.json'); assert rj.kind=='fix_report' and rj.attempt==1 and rj.nonce; assert DirtyFiles()==[] and head==base

requirements.title: The fix report kind and questions
requirements.rationale: The brain's only output is one validated report or one question, and `af` builds every effect from it plus its own measurements.

criteria.action: register as submission kind `fix_report` with tool name `submit_fix`, and accept exactly one of two forms: the question form (`question {text 1–2000 chars, options 0–6 strings of 1–200 chars, root_cause? ≤ 8000 chars}`) or the report form (no `question`)
criteria.contract: Name is `fix_report` and ToolName is `submit_fix`; the question form and the report form are accepted; the mixed payload is refused

setup: the FixReport kind
check.pseudocode: assert K.Name=='fix_report' and K.ToolName=='submit_fix'; assert ok(K.Validate(q)); assert ok(K.Validate(rep)); assert problems(K.Validate(mixed))

criteria.action: enforce on the report form: `type` one of fix|feat|refactor|perf|docs|test|chore; `subject` 1–72 chars, one line, no trailing period, no leading `<type>:`; `root_cause` and `change` 1–4000 chars each; `files` 1–500 unique `{path, why}` with a valid relative slash path not under `.git/` or `.agent-fox/` and `why` 1–300 chars; `tests` 0–100 `{path, name?, proves}` where path is a regular file in the submitted tree; `criteria` 0–50 `{criterion, status met|unmet|partial|not_applicable, evidence}`; `decisions` 0–30 strings of at most 500 chars
criteria.contract: values inside the limit are accepted; values outside produce a problem naming that field; a test path that is not a regular file in the submitted tree is refused

setup: a valid baseline report and question
check.pseudocode: for (field,okv,badv) in CASES: assert ok(Validate(set(base,field,okv))); assert field in names(Validate(set(base,field,badv)))

criteria.condition: a payload has unknown fields or breaks one or more field rules
criteria.action: refuse the payload and name every problem in one response
criteria.contract: `Validate` returns one `Problem` per violation and no normalised payload; no submission file is written

setup: a payload with an unknown field `extra`, an empty subject, a duplicate file path and an invalid criterion status
check.pseudocode: out, probs = K.Validate(bad); assert out is None and len(probs)>=4; assert not exists(runDir/'submission.json')

criteria.action: for any accepted payload, return a normalised payload with trimmed strings, LF line endings instead of CRLF, `type` defaulted to `fix`, and `files` sorted by path, such that validating the normalised payload again returns it unchanged
criteria.contract: strings are trimmed with no CR left; type is `fix` when omitted; files are sorted by path; validating the normalised payload returns it unchanged

setup: any accepted payload
check.pseudocode: for p in gen_valid_reports(): n = Validate(p); assert '\r' not in n and n.type and is_sorted(n.files, key=path); assert Validate(n) == n

criteria.condition: the loop receives an accepted question submission
criteria.action: end the run without applying the brain's tree, creating a branch or commit, or touching the checkout
criteria.contract: status `needs_human`, exit code 3, with the question, options labelled `A`, `B`, … in order, and the shell's `resume`

setup: a scripted brain whose first submission is a question with options `x`, `y` and `z`
a repository with a recorded tree and branches
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==3 and r.status=='needs_human'; assert [o.id for o in r.options]==['A','B','C'] and r.resume.argv; assert branches==['main'] and head==base and DirtyFiles()==[]

criteria.condition: `af fix land` finds a question submission for the run
criteria.action: refuse to land, telling the person to re-run `af fix brief <input> --context <answer>`
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `submission`, exit code 1

setup: a run whose submission.json is a question form
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix land', id); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='submission'; assert 'af fix brief' in r.message and '--context' in r.message; assert branches==['main']

requirements.title: Applying the brain's tree to the host
requirements.rationale: The host checkout holds exactly what will be measured and committed, and a commit made inside the box never reaches the branch.

criteria.condition: `brain.Execute` accepts a round's submission
criteria.action: export the box with `Session.Export` and write to the host every exported file outside `.git/` and `.agent-fox/` and not ignored by the host's git rules, when the host file is absent or differs in content, mode or symlink target. Symlinks are recreated, never followed
criteria.contract: new, changed and mode-changed files are written, and the symlink is recreated as a symlink without following it; nothing from .git/, .agent-fox/ or build/ reaches the host; the ledger holds `apply {written, deleted, ignored}`; `git rev-parse HEAD` equals base_head, so the in-box commit is absent

setup: a host checkout with .gitignore containing `build/`
an export with a new file, a changed file, a mode change, a symlink, a commit made inside the box, plus files under .git/, .agent-fox/ and build/
check.pseudocode: res = Apply(host, exportDir); assert read(host/'new')==...; assert islink(host/'ln') and readlink==target; assert not exists(host/'build/x'); assert ledger.last.kind=='apply'; assert rev_parse('HEAD')==base_head

criteria.condition: a file in the host's `checks.FileView` is absent from the export
criteria.action: delete that file from the host checkout
criteria.contract: old.txt is deleted from the host; the apply ledger entry counts one deleted

setup: a host checkout with tracked file `old.txt` and an export lacking it
check.pseudocode: Apply(host, export); assert not exists(host/'old.txt'); assert ledger.apply.deleted==1

criteria.action: for any exported tree, leave the host file view, minus ignored paths, equal in paths, contents, modes and symlink targets to the export minus `.git/` and `.agent-fox/`
criteria.contract: the host file view minus ignored paths equals the export minus .git/ and .agent-fox/ in paths, content, mode and symlink target

setup: a host checkout with random tracked files and ignored paths
check.pseudocode: for (hostTree, exportTree) in gen(): Apply(); assert snapshot(FileView(host) - ignored) == snapshot(export - {'.git','.agent-fox'})

criteria.condition: the export contains no files
criteria.action: apply nothing to the host
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `sandbox`; host tree unchanged

setup: a host checkout with files and an empty export
check.pseudocode: err = Apply(host, emptyExport); assert err.category=='sandbox'; assert snapshot(host)==before

criteria.action: record the ledger entry `apply {written, deleted, ignored}` after each apply, and never commit during rounds, so HEAD stays at `base_head` and no commit the brain made inside the box reaches the host
criteria.contract: `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `base_head` after every apply

criteria.condition: a measured round is followed by another round
criteria.action: re-sync the box from the host checkout with `Session.Sync`, so the box holds the measured tree with protected paths reverted
criteria.contract: the box at the start of round 2 holds the host tree, with `.specs/x.md` reverted to base content; Session.Sync was called between the rounds

setup: a two-round scripted run whose first round edits `.specs/x.md` and a source file and fails the gate
check.pseudocode: onRun(round=2): assert read(box/'.specs/x.md')==base_content and read(box/'src.go')==round1_content

criteria.condition: a round ends without an accepted submission
criteria.action: apply nothing from that round's box to the host
criteria.contract: host tree unchanged by that round

setup: a scripted brain whose round edits files and ends without submitting
check.pseudocode: run(fix, script=edit_no_submit); assert snapshot(host)==before; assert 'apply' not in kinds(ledger)

requirements.title: Measuring
requirements.rationale: Every effect is decided from facts `af` measured on the host itself, never from the brain's claims.

criteria.condition: at measure time the current branch is not the base or HEAD differs from `base_head`
criteria.action: stop without landing or parking, naming the commits since `base_head`
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `git`, exit code 1

setup: a run whose host HEAD advanced by a commit made outside af, then one whose current branch is not the base
check.pseudocode: commit_outside(); r = run('fix land'); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='git' and subj in r.message; assert branches==['main'] or only foreign

criteria.condition: a path from `gitx.ChangedPaths(base_head)` lies under a protected path
criteria.action: restore that path to its content at `base_head`, or delete it when it did not exist there, and list it in `reverted_paths`
criteria.contract: warning `protected_path_reverted` per path

setup: a host tree with a modified `.specs/a.md` (existing at base), a new `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and a source change
check.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert read('.specs/a.md')==base and not exists('.github/workflows/ci.yml'); assert set(m.reverted)=={...}; assert count(warnings,'protected_path_reverted')==2

criteria.condition: no changed path remains after the protected-path revert
criteria.action: produce the refusal `no_change` without running the gate
criteria.contract: refusal kind `no_change`

setup: a tree whose only change is under .specs/
check.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert m.refusal.kind=='no_change'; assert gateRuns==baselineOnly

criteria.condition: the report's `files` differ from the measured changed paths
criteria.action: list the undeclared changes and the declared-but-unchanged paths in `scope {undeclared, unchanged}` without refusing
criteria.contract: warning `scope_mismatch`

setup: a report declaring files a.go and b.go, while git shows a.go and c.go changed
check.pseudocode: s = Scope(declared=['a.go','b.go'], changed=['a.go','c.go']); assert s.undeclared==['c.go'] and s.unchanged==['b.go']; assert not refused

criteria.condition: changed paths remain and `--no-verify` is not set
criteria.action: run `checks.Run(dir, {Table: pinned})` and compare it with the baseline by gate id using `checks.Compare`. Under `--no-verify`, skip this step and set the verdict to `unverified`
criteria.contract: `after {gate_id, passed}`, `verdict` and `landable` in the result

setup: a repository with the Makefile fixture gate green at baseline
a change that keeps it green
check.pseudocode: m = Measure(); assert m.after.gate_id != baseline.gate_id and m.landable; m2 = Measure(noVerify); assert m2.verdict=='unverified' and m2.after is None

criteria.condition: the verdict is landable and `--no-verify` is not set
criteria.action: run `conform.Check(dir, since=base_head)` with the pinned table, set `closes` true only for outcome `proven`, and let every other outcome land with `Refs`
criteria.contract: `revert_check {outcome, reason}`; warning `fix_not_proven` when the outcome is not `proven`

setup: a landable change with a proving test
a landable change whose test passes without the fix
a regressed change
check.pseudocode: assert Measure(proven).closes and not Measure(notProven).closes; assert 'fix_not_proven' in codes(w); assert conformCalls(regressed)==0

criteria.condition: the loop measures a non-landable verdict or `no_change`
criteria.action: record ledger entries `measure {verdict, after_gate_id, revert_outcome, closes, changed, reverted}` and `refusal {kind}`, and put the refusal kind, the verdict, each failing check's name and tail (at most 4 KiB each) and the reverted paths into the next round's task block
criteria.contract: the ledger holds `measure {verdict, after_gate_id, revert_outcome, closes, changed, reverted}` and `refusal {kind}`; the next task block holds the refusal kind, verdict, each failing check's name and a tail of at most 4096 bytes, and the reverted paths

setup: a round whose change regresses a check producing 10 KiB of output and also touches .specs/
check.pseudocode: assert ledger has measure and refusal; t = nextTask; assert 'regressed' in t and checkName in t and len(tail_in(t))<=4096 and '.specs/' in t

criteria.condition: `af fix land` measures a refusal
criteria.action: park the work as in 09-REQ-9 without starting any brain round
criteria.contract: status `unverified`, exit code 4

setup: a checkout edited by hand that leaves the gate red, with a valid submission
check.pseudocode: r = run('fix land', id); assert r.exit==4 and r.result.outcome=='parked'; assert subject(branch_head).startswith('wip:'); assert brain.runs==0

requirements.title: Attempts, rounds and bounds
requirements.rationale: A refused brain keeps its attempt's remaining budget instead of getting a fresh one, and work is never lost when bounds or the deadline run out.

criteria.action: run at most `--attempts` attempts, each with `--budget` USD and `--max-turns` turns, and pass the run-wide round sequence number as `Brief.Attempt` for each `brain.Execute` call
criteria.contract: result fields `attempts`, `rounds` and `attempts_max`

setup: a spy brain recording Brief.Attempt, and a scenario with two refused rounds in attempt 1 and one round in attempt 2
check.pseudocode: assert spy.attempts==[1,2,3]; assert (r.attempts,r.rounds,r.attempts_max)==(2,3,2); assert len(glob('brief.*.md'))==3

criteria.condition: a measured refusal occurs within an attempt
criteria.action: start another round in the same attempt with the attempt's remaining cost and turns, only while more than USD 0 remains, at least 1 turn remains, and at least 1 minute of brain time remains. Brain time is the time left until the command deadline minus a measuring reserve of 3 × the baseline gate's duration + 1 minute
criteria.contract: with cost > 0, turns ≥ 1 and brain time ≥ 1 minute, another round starts with the remaining cost and turns; cost 0, 0 turns, or less than 1 minute of brain time ends the attempt; brain time is deadline-left minus the reserve

setup: a measured refusal with remaining budget cases: cost 0, 0 turns, and a command deadline leaving less than 1 minute after reserve = 3 × baseline duration + 1 minute
check.pseudocode: assert Continue(cost=1,turns=5,left=10m,baseline=1m)==True; assert Continue(cost=0,...)==False; assert Continue(turns=0)==False; assert Continue(left=4m,baseline=1m)==False; assert BrainTime(10m,1m)==6m

criteria.condition: an attempt ends because its bounds are spent or a round ended without an accepted submission, and attempts remain
criteria.action: start the next attempt from the current host tree with a fresh budget and a fresh brain context, and state in its first task block why the previous attempt ended
criteria.contract: attempt 2's first brain context starts from the host tree containing attempt 1's change; its budget and turns equal the full per-attempt values; its first task block states why attempt 1 ended

setup: attempt 1's bounds spent after an applied change that leaves the gate red
check.pseudocode: assert spy[2].box_has('change.go'); assert spy[2].MaxCostUSD==10 and spy[2].MaxTurns==150; assert 'bounds' in spy[2].Task

criteria.condition: `brain.Execute` returns a failure it marked non-retryable (for example `budget`, `auth`, or a non-retryable `sandbox` failure)
criteria.action: start no further attempt
criteria.contract: the run proceeds to 09-REQ-7.5 with that failure as the last round's failure

setup: brain.Execute failing with category budget on attempt 1, with attempts remaining; same for auth
check.pseudocode: r = loop(exec=fail('budget',retryable=false)); assert exec.calls==1; assert r.category=='budget'

criteria.condition: no attempt remains without a landable verdict
criteria.action: park the applied change when the host tree holds one, using the last accepted report's subject and raising the warning `attempt_failed` when the last round failed. Fail with the last round's failure when nothing was applied
criteria.contract: parked: status `unverified`, exit 4; nothing applied: status `failed` with the last round's category, exit 1

setup: scenario A: attempt 1 applied a red change, attempt 2's round failed
scenario B: every round failed before any apply
check.pseudocode: a = run(A); assert a.exit==4 and 'attempt_failed' in codes(a.warnings) and wip_subject==lastSubject; b = run(B); assert b.exit==1 and b.category==lastFailure.category and branches==['main']

criteria.condition: the context is cancelled or the command deadline passes during the run
criteria.action: park any applied change locally, without push or forge write, on a context detached from cancellation and bounded to 10 seconds, or discard it under `--dry-run`, then return the context error to the shell
criteria.contract: status `failed` with category `cancelled` or `timeout`; the parked branch, when one was made, exists locally only

setup: a run with an applied change when the context is cancelled mid-round; same for a short --timeout; same with --dry-run
a local bare origin and a recording forge
check.pseudocode: cancel(); r = run(); assert r.category in ['cancelled','timeout']; assert local_branch_exists and not remote_branch_exists; assert writes(forge)==[]; dry = run('--dry-run'); assert branches==['main'] and DirtyFiles()==[]

criteria.action: hold one box across every round through `box.With`, close it on every exit path including failure and cancellation, and report spec 07's `Tally` across all rounds as the envelope `usage`
criteria.contract: the box opens once per run and closes exactly once on success, failure and cancellation; the envelope usage equals the summed Tally of all rounds

setup: a box provider spy counting opens and closes, and a brain reporting cost and turns per round
check.pseudocode: assert (spy.opens,spy.closes)==(1,1) for each scenario; assert env.usage == sum(round.usage)

requirements.title: Landing
requirements.rationale: A measured, landable change becomes exactly one commit that `af` made, on a fresh branch, with a pull-request body rendered from facts.

criteria.condition: a text or file input reaches landing or parking and `--land pr` is set
criteria.action: create exactly one issue in the target repository whose title is the report subject and whose body is the original input under `## Original report`, followed by a line naming the run
criteria.contract: `issue_created {number, url}`, the artifact `issue`, and the side effect `create_issue` with status `done`

setup: an httptest GitHub forge and a file ./bug.md
check.pseudocode: assert count(forge, 'POST issues')==1; assert body.title==subject and '## Original report' in body.body and runId in body.body; assert r.issue_created.number and 'issue' in artifacts

criteria.action: name the branch `fix/<N>-<slug>` for an issue, or `fix/<slug>` without one, where slug is `gitx.Slug` of the issue title (or of the subject for text and file input). Make the name unique with `gitx.UniqueBranchName` and create it from `base_head`, carrying the working tree along
criteria.contract: the `branch` artifact and side effect

setup: an issue #42 titled `Crash on empty input`
a text input with subject `Handle nil`
an existing local branch and a remote branch with the same name
check.pseudocode: assert BranchFor(issue42)=='fix/42-crash-on-empty-input'; assert BranchFor(text)=='fix/handle-nil'; assert BranchFor(issue42, existing) != existing; assert merge_base(branch, base_head)==base_head

criteria.condition: the verdict is landable, or `--no-verify` is set and the result was measured
criteria.action: commit with `gitx.CommitAll` using the message `<type>: <subject>`, a blank line, `change` capped at 2000 bytes, a blank line, `Closes <url>` (when `closes`) or `Refs <url>` when there is an issue, and a blank line followed by `Agent-Fox-Run: <run id>` as the last paragraph
criteria.contract: exactly one commit on the branch above `base_head`; `commit` holds its full hash

setup: a landable proven result with a 3000-byte `change`, type `feat`, subject `Add x`, issue URL
a landable not-proven result
check.pseudocode: msg = git_log('-1','%B'); paras = msg.split('\n\n'); assert paras[0]=='feat: Add x' and len(paras[1])<=2000 and paras[-2].startswith('Closes ') and paras[-1]=='Agent-Fox-Run: '+rid; assert count(base_head..HEAD)==1

criteria.condition: a commit hook makes the landing commit fail
criteria.action: park the work as in 09-REQ-9
criteria.contract: warning `commit_hook_failed`; status `unverified`, exit 4

setup: a repository with a pre-commit hook that exits 1
a landable change
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==4 and 'commit_hook_failed' in codes(r.warnings); assert subject(branch).startswith('wip:'); assert DirtyFiles()==[]

criteria.condition: the push of the branch still fails after `Push(ctx, branch, 3, log)` retries
criteria.action: keep the branch and commit locally, return the checkout to the base branch, and raise the warning `push_retried` for each retry
criteria.contract: status `failed`, category `git`, exit 1; `next` holds `git push -u origin <branch>`

setup: an origin whose push is rejected with a transient error each time
gitx sleep disabled for the test
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==1 and r.category=='git'; assert count(warnings,'push_retried')==2; assert 'git push -u origin '+branch in r.next; assert current_branch()=='main'

criteria.condition: the branch was pushed and `--land pr` is set
criteria.action: call `CreatePullRequest(target, {Title: "<type>: <subject>", Body, Head: branch, Base: base, Draft})` with Draft true under `--no-verify` or when any criterion is `unmet` or `partial`. When the call fails after the push, still finish as `done`
criteria.contract: `pull_request {number, url, draft}`; warning `criteria_unmet` when drafted for criteria; on failure, warning `pull_request_failed` carrying the forge error, and `pull_request` null

setup: an httptest GitHub forge
a report with a criterion `partial`
a variant where the PR creation returns 500
check.pseudocode: assert req.draft and 'criteria_unmet' in codes(w); assert not req2.draft; r3 = run(forge500); assert r3.exit==0 and 'pull_request_failed' in codes(r3.warnings) and r3.result.pull_request is None

criteria.action: for any report, render the pull-request body in this order: a marker comment with the run id; the verification section labelled measured by af (per-check baseline and after table, verdict, revert-check outcome and reason, reverted paths); the root cause, change, tests, criteria and decisions labelled reported; the changed files from git with their `why` or "(not declared)"; the `Closes`/`Refs` line; a footer with run id, brain and cost with source. Keep the body within `issuex.MaxBodyLength` by cutting the reported sections first behind a visible marker, never cutting the verification section or the `Closes`/`Refs` line, and write it with `RunDir.WriteReport`
criteria.contract: `report.md` equals the body and is the `report` artifact

setup: forge limits of 65536 and 1048576
check.pseudocode: for (rep, limit) in gen(): b = RenderBody(rep, limit); assert len(b)<=limit; assert order(b, MARKERS); assert verification(b)==full and refsLine in b; if cut: assert CUT_MARKER in b

criteria.condition: landing completes
criteria.action: return the checkout to the base branch with a clean tree
criteria.contract: status `done`, exit 0, outcome `landed`; under `--no-verify`, status `unverified`, exit 4, with warning `not_verified`

setup: a landable result, and the same input with --no-verify
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==0 and r.result.outcome=='landed' and current_branch()=='main'; r2 = run(fix,'--no-verify'); assert r2.exit==4 and 'not_verified' in codes(r2.warnings)

requirements.title: Parking, land modes and dry runs
requirements.rationale: Work that does not land is never thrown away, and nothing is written that the mode did not ask for.

criteria.condition: a result is parked (non-landable after the last attempt or in `fix land`, interrupted run, or failed landing commit)
criteria.action: create the 09-REQ-8.2 branch and commit with `gitx.CommitAllNoVerify` using the message `wip: <subject>`, a blank line, `Parked by af fix: verdict <v>` with the failing checks, a blank line, `Refs <url>` when there is an issue, and a blank line followed by the `Agent-Fox-Run: <run id>` trailer
criteria.contract: the branch uses the 09-REQ-8.2 name; the message is `wip: <subject>`, a blank line, `Parked by af fix: verdict <v>` with the failing checks, a blank line, `Refs <url>`, a blank line, `Agent-Fox-Run: <run id>`; the commit was made without running the failing hook

setup: a red result for an issue with a pre-commit hook that fails
check.pseudocode: msg = git_log(branch,'%B'); assert msg.startswith('wip: '); assert 'Parked by af fix: verdict still_failing' in msg and 'Refs '+url in msg and msg.endswith('Agent-Fox-Run: '+rid)

criteria.condition: a result is parked and the run was not interrupted
criteria.action: push the branch unless `--land none`, and under `--land pr` open a draft pull request that says `Refs`, creating the issue first for text and file input as in 09-REQ-8.1
criteria.contract: `pull_request.draft` is true and the body contains `Refs <issue url>`

setup: a red result from text input and an httptest GitHub forge
a variant with --land branch and one interrupted by cancellation
check.pseudocode: assert remote_has(branch) and pr.draft and 'Refs '+issue_url in pr.body; assert order(forge.requests)[0]=='POST issues'; assert writes(forge_branch_mode)==[]

criteria.condition: parking completes
criteria.action: return the checkout to the base branch with a clean tree
criteria.contract: status `unverified`, exit 4, outcome `parked`, warning `fix_not_landed` naming the verdict; `next` holds `git switch <branch>`

setup: a red result that parks
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix); assert r.exit==4 and r.result.outcome=='parked'; assert 'fix_not_landed' in codes(r.warnings) and verdict in msg; assert 'git switch '+r.result.branch in r.next; assert DirtyFiles()==[]

criteria.condition: `--land none` is set
criteria.action: make the local branch and commit, push nothing, and send no forge request
criteria.contract: `pushed` false, `pull_request` null; the forge test server records zero requests

setup: a local bare origin and a recording httptest forge
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--land','none'); assert local_branch_exists and not origin_has(branch); assert r.result.pushed==False and r.result.pull_request is None; assert forge.landing_requests==[]

criteria.condition: `--dry-run` is set
criteria.action: run everything up to the landing decision, then discard the applied change with `ResetHard(base_head)` and `Clean`, create no branch or commit, push nothing, list `branch`, `commit` and `push` as `planned` side effects, and refuse forge writes through spec 05's `DryRunForge`
criteria.contract: the status the real run would have had, outcome `dry_run`; the forge test server records zero write requests

setup: a landable fix and a recording httptest forge
check.pseudocode: r = run(fix,'--dry-run'); assert r.result.outcome=='dry_run' and r.exit==0; assert branches==['main'] and head==base_head and DirtyFiles()==[]; assert planned(r) >= {'branch','commit','push','create_pull_request'}; assert writes(forge)==[]

criteria.action: for any run that ends `landed`, `parked`, `needs_human` or `dry_run`, leave the base branch checked out at `base_head` with `gitx.DirtyFiles` empty
criteria.contract: the current branch is the base branch; the working tree is clean; for needs_human and dry_run, HEAD equals base_head

setup: scripted scenarios
check.pseudocode: for sc in scenarios(): r = run(sc); assert current_branch()==base and DirtyFiles()==[]; if r.outcome in ['needs_human','dry_run']: assert head==base_head

requirements.title: Result, multi-round scripted brain, offline tests and documentation
requirements.rationale: Callers consume one stable result shape, refusal-then-fix must be testable offline, and outdated docs count as regressions.

criteria.action: emit for `fix` and `fix land` a result with run_id, issue (url or null), issue_created ({number, url} or null), base, base_head, attempts, rounds, attempts_max, outcome (landed|parked|needs_human|failed|dry_run), verdict, landable, closes, baseline and after ({gate_id, passed}), revert_check ({outcome, reason} or null), changed_files, reverted_paths, scope ({undeclared, unchanged}), land, branch, commit (full hash), pushed, pull_request ({number, url, draft} or null) and box ({provider, image, network}, with network `host` for `local`)
criteria.contract: the result validates against the declared `fix` / `fix_land` result schema

setup: a landed result and a parked result for an issue input, and the declared `fix` and `fix land` result schemas
check.pseudocode: for r in [landed, parked]: assert validate(schema, r.result); assert r.result.box.network=='host'; assert r.result.commit matches [0-9a-f]{40}

criteria.action: report the artifacts `branch`, `commit`, `pull_request`, `issue` (when created), `report`, `submission`, `transcript` and `run_dir`, and the side effects `branch`, `commit`, `push`, `create_issue` and `create_pull_request`, each with status `done`, `planned` or `failed`
criteria.contract: the landed run lists artifacts branch, commit, pull_request, report, submission, transcript and run_dir (and issue when created); side effects branch, commit, push, create_issue and create_pull_request are `done` for landed, `planned` for dry-run, and the push is `failed` for the push failure

setup: a landed run, a dry run and a run whose push failed
check.pseudocode: assert {'branch','commit','pull_request','report','submission','transcript','run_dir'} <= kinds(landed.artifacts); assert status(dry,'push')=='planned'; assert status(pushfail,'push')=='failed'

criteria.condition: the scripted brain is given a script of the form `{"rounds": [{"steps": [...]}, ...]}`
criteria.action: replay round k on the k-th `Run` call on the same brain value, end at once with outcome `ended` on any call past the last round, and treat a plain `{"steps": [...]}` file as one round
criteria.contract: call 1 replays round 1 and call 2 replays round 2; call 3 ends at once with outcome `ended`; the plain script behaves as one round: the second call ends at once

setup: a script `{"rounds": [{"steps": [...A]}, {"steps": [...B]}]}` and a plain `{"steps": [...]}` script
check.pseudocode: b = Scripted(multi); assert run(b).steps==A; assert run(b).steps==B; assert run(b).outcome=='ended' and no steps; p = Scripted(plain); run(p); assert run(p).outcome=='ended'

criteria.action: run offline in `make check` with no vendor key, using temporary repositories with a local bare `origin`, a Makefile `check` fixture gate (skipped when `make` is absent), `httptest` GitHub and GitLab forges injected through `App.NewForge`, `--sandbox local`, scripted scripts, and `provider/faux` for the agentkit path
criteria.contract: `make check` exits 0 with no network access beyond loopback

setup: no vendor key in the environment
an httptest GitLab injected through App.NewForge, a temporary repo with a local bare origin and the Makefile fixture gate
check.pseudocode: unsetenv(vendor keys); r = run(fix,'--brain','agentkit','--model','provider/faux'); assert r.exit==0 and gitlabMR.created; assert all(conn.is_loopback)

criteria.action: describe the toolbelt flow `af fix brief` → work → `af fix submit` → `af fix land`; keep the method (read, refuse early, diagnose, test first, verify with targeted tests and `af gate run`); state that the agent never commits, pushes, branches or edits the issue; and use the branch form `fix/<N>-<slug>`
criteria.contract: the skill text contains no instruction to run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout -b` or to open a pull request

setup: skills/af-fix text
check.pseudocode: t = read('skills/af-fix/SKILL.md'); assert order(t,'af fix brief','af fix submit','af fix land'); assert 'fix/<N>-<slug>' in t; for bad in ['git commit','git push','git checkout -b']: assert bad not in instructions(t)

criteria.action: describe in `docs/cli.md` the five commands, their flags, defaults, results, warnings, the `preflight` category and exit codes; in `docs/configuration.md` the box-side `gate.json` and `guard.json` and the token for `--land pr`; in `docs/model-usage.md` the per-attempt bounds, attempts, rounds, and that dry runs spend model money; in `docs/architecture.md` the fix loop, the apply and measure steps, the `fix.json` and `report.md` run files and the `codefix` row; and in `README.md` the `internal/fix/` package
criteria.contract: cli.md lists the five commands, flags, defaults, warnings, the `preflight` category and exit codes; configuration.md mentions gate.json, guard.json and the token for --land pr; model-usage.md describes per-attempt bounds, attempts, rounds and that dry runs spend model money; architecture.md describes the fix loop, apply and measure, fix.json, report.md and the codefix row; README.md mentions internal/fix/

setup: docs/cli.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/model-usage.md, docs/architecture.md and README.md
check.pseudocode: for (file, needles) in DOCS: for n in needles: assert n in read(file)

execution_paths.title: An issue URL becomes a landed pull request

steps.action: runs `af fix <issue URL> --brain scripted --sandbox local --dir <repo>`
resolves the issue input through the forge and opens a run directory
checks the work tree, branch, clean tree, gate, origin, forge and brain, runs the baseline gate, and writes fix.json
renders the brief, opens the local box, writes gate.json and guard.json, and calls brain.Execute
edits the tree in the box (and commits there) and submits a fix report through submit_fix
mirrors the exported tree onto the host checkout without .git
reverts protected paths, runs the gate after, gets a landable verdict, and runs the revert check
creates fix/<N>-<slug> from base_head, commits once with the Agent-Fox-Run trailer, pushes to origin, and opens a pull request saying Closes or Refs
prints status done, exits 0, with the checkout back on the base branch and a clean tree

setup: a temporary repository on main with a local bare origin and the Makefile fixture gate
an httptest GitHub serving the issue and accepting the pull request
a scripted brain that edits the tree, commits inside the box and submits a report with a proving test
end_state: status done and exit 0
`fix/<N>-<slug>` exists with exactly one commit above base whose last paragraph is `Agent-Fox-Run: <run id>`
the commit the brain made in the box is not on the branch
the branch is pushed to origin
one pull request is opened with body containing `Closes <issue url>`
the checkout is on main with a clean tree

execution_paths.title: A file report creates an issue and a pull request

steps.action: runs `af fix ./bug.md --repo o/r --brain scripted --sandbox local --land pr`
runs preflight, the baseline, one round, apply and measure with a landable verdict
creates one issue from the report under ## Original report
creates fix/<N>-<slug>, commits, pushes, and opens a pull request saying Closes or Refs that issue
emits status done with issue_created and pull_request set

setup: a temporary repository with local bare origin and fixture gate
an httptest GitHub and ./bug.md
end_state: status done
exactly one issue was created with the report under `## Original report`
a branch is pushed and one pull request body says `Closes` or `Refs` followed by the new issue URL
issue_created and pull_request are set in the result

execution_paths.title: A refusal becomes the next round, and the second change lands

steps.action: runs `af fix <issue URL>` with a two-round scripted script
submits a first change that makes the gate regress
returns the refusal with verdict regressed and the failing checks' tails
re-syncs the box and starts round 2 in the same attempt, with the refusal in the task block
submits a second change that passes
commits, pushes and opens the pull request
emits status done with rounds 2

setup: a fixture repo with green baseline
a two-round scripted script: round 1 breaks the gate, round 2 fixes it
an httptest GitHub
end_state: round 2's task block contains the verdict `regressed` and the failing checks' output
the run lands with status done and exit 0
the envelope reports rounds 2 and attempts 1
the pull request is opened

execution_paths.title: Unverified work is parked as a draft

steps.action: runs `af fix <issue URL> --land pr --attempts 1` with a script whose change leaves the gate red
refuses with a still-failing verdict, and the attempt's bounds are spent
creates the branch, commits wip: <subject> without hooks, pushes it, and opens a draft pull request saying Refs
emits status unverified, exit 4, warning fix_not_landed, with the base branch checked out and a clean tree

setup: a fixture repo, a script whose change leaves the gate red
an httptest GitHub, a local bare origin
end_state: status unverified and exit 4 with warning `fix_not_landed`
a `wip: …` commit on the fix branch pushed to origin
a draft pull request whose body says `Refs <issue url>`
the base branch is checked out with a clean tree

execution_paths.title: A question stops the run and the answer resumes it

steps.action: runs `af fix <issue URL>` with a script whose submission carries a question
ends the run without applying the tree, creating a branch or commit
emits status needs_human, exit 3, with options A, B and resume.argv
re-runs resume.argv with `--context B` appended
finds the earlier run by input key and context count, and renders the same prefix_sha256 with the question and answer B in the task block

setup: a fixture repo and an httptest GitHub
a script whose submission is a question with options
end_state: the first run exits 3 with options A, B and resume.argv, with no branch or commit and an untouched tree
the resumed run's brief has the same prefix_sha256
its task block holds the earlier question and the answer `B`

steps.action: runs `af fix <issue URL> --dry-run` against an httptest forge
runs preflight, the baseline, the round, apply and measure up to the landing decision
discards the applied change with ResetHard(base_head) and Clean
refuses the pull-request write and lists it as planned
emits the real run's status with branch, commit, push and create_pull_request planned, and zero forge write requests

setup: a fixture repo with local bare origin and an httptest GitHub recording writes
a scripted brain submitting a landable fix
end_state: zero write requests reached the forge
no branch and no commit were created, nothing was pushed
branch, commit, push and create_pull_request are listed as `planned`
the tree is clean at base_head and the status is the real run's

execution_paths.title: A person fixes at their own checkout

steps.action: runs `af fix brief <issue URL>` and receives brief_path and the submit argv
edits files directly in the checkout
pipes a fix report into `af fix submit --run-id <id>`
measures once, then commits on fix/<N>-<slug>, pushes, and opens the pull request
emits status done with the checkout back on the base branch

setup: a fixture repo with local bare origin and an httptest GitHub
end_state: brief returns brief_path and the submit argv
submit is accepted
land measures once and creates `fix/<N>-<slug>` with one commit, pushes, and opens a pull request
status done and the checkout is back on the base branch
